$comment: The recorded state of the `endora new instance` acceptance criterion
(`specs/110-instance-repository/` FR-011, contracts/instance-repository.md §6, T140).
`acceptance:instance:ci` compares a run to this file and fails on drift in EITHER
direction: a newly-red assertion fails, and so does a newly-green one nobody recorded.
An unrecorded pass is a criterion whose meaning moved without anybody reading it.
IT LANDED WITH TWO REDS AND EIGHT UNMEASURED, AND THAT WAS THE FINDING RATHER THAN A
SHORTFALL OF THE INSTRUMENT. Before this file existed nothing had ever run a scaffolded
instance: `packages/cli/test/new-instance.test.ts` asserts the plan, and the merge
request before it (!1580) took the created backend to `tsc` exit 0 and said in as
many words that a type-check was the whole of the evidence. The first run of this
criterion found that the tree compiles, installs, and then does nothing at all.
T141 REPAIRED FOUR OF THE FIVE DEFECTS THAT RUN FOUND, and A3's reason below is now a
different and much narrower sentence than the one it landed with. What is left is one
of the five — reported to the orchestrator rather than repaired, because it is a schema
decision: the platform's own migration corpus is not self-contained.
EVERY NON-PASS ENTRY BELOW NAMES THE CONTRACT OR TASK IT WAITS ON, AND THAT RULE IS
ENFORCED RATHER THAN INTENDED. `expectationRefusals` in
`../scripts/acceptance/instance-assertions.ts` refuses this file — exit 2, not a drift —
when a non-`pass` entry carries no reason, or a reason that names neither a task (T###)
nor a contract, or one of the four spellings of the word the row calls out:
`unimplemented`, `not implemented`, `TODO`, `not started`.
THE `registry` MODE IS `unrun` AND NOT AN EMPTY `recorded`. A supply route nobody has
measured owes no assertion states, and writing a prediction of them is the thing this
file exists to refuse. The first run with ENDORA_NPM_REGISTRY set drifts — naming every
assertion it measured — which is what makes that record arrive from a measurement.
THERE ARE FOURTEEN ASSERTIONS AND THE NUMBERING IS SETTLED. `instance-repository.md`
R6.3 numbers A1…A13, its A13 being FR-023/SC-011's built-admin-stylesheet assertion;
`instance-tree.md` §6 opens by declaring the criterion to be §6's UNCHANGED plus one
assertion it adds, so the two share one namespace and an extension is not entitled to
renumber its base. A13 stays R6.3's and the wiring bound is A14. `instance-repository.md`
R6.3a is where the list is now declared to live, and it names its one extension.

A1.reason: The command's own `outwardReferences` derivation over the tree it wrote finds nothing naming anything above it. Evaluated before this run pins anything: publication's stand-in writes `file:` specifiers naming a directory outside the instance, and those are the harness's.

A2.reason: `pnpm install` succeeds outside the checkout, from packed tarballs, with no symlink back. The pinning is the closure of what the instance declares rather than the declaration itself — measured, a `pnpm install` fetches four module packages the manifest never names, as non-optional peers of packages it does, and an override does not reach an auto-installed peer.

A3.reason: THE DEFECT IT LANDED ON IS REPAIRED AND A NARROWER ONE IS UNDERNEATH IT. `pnpm run migrate` really runs now — T141 gave every root script `pnpm -C backend` instead of a `--filter <name>` that matched no project and exited 0, and gave an instance the platform's own twelve migrations and six entities, which `coreEntries: []` and `coreEntities: []` meant it ran none of. What it fails on is the schema itself: `Migration20260430T170044CoreSalesChannelsPromote` creates `sales_channel_cms_pages` with a foreign key to `cms_pages`, which `cms` owns and which the default module set does not include. THE PLATFORM'S OWN MIGRATION CORPUS IS NOT SELF-CONTAINED: two of its twelve migrations reach into seven modules' tables (that one into `cms_pages`, `customer_accounts`, `organizations`, `promotions`, `quote_requests` and `taxes`; `Migration20260717T134752CoreTenantScopeIndexes` into `analytics_events` and `newsletter_subscribers`), and a fourth edge is module-to-module — `webhooks`' migration creates the `api_keys` table that `api_keys`' and `orders`' own migrations then alter. Measured by hand on a set with `cms`, `analytics`, `newsletter` and `webhooks` added: 119 migrations apply, exit 0. Reported to the orchestrator rather than repaired in T141 — moving schema out of an applied migration in the frozen baseline prefix is a decision `contracts/instance-migration-order.md` and `specs/097-migration-sql-boundary/contracts/migration-cross-module-sql.md` both bear on, and widening the default set would hide it rather than answer it.

A4.reason: There is no migrated schema to boot against: A3 fails, so `bootOnce` is not attempted. IT WAS `fail` BEFORE T141 AND THE CHANGE IS HONESTY, NOT A REGRESSION — the migrate step used to exit 0 having done nothing, so the criterion went on to a boot that could not work; now the migration genuinely fails and the criterion says so once. Three of the four defects recorded here at T140 are repaired and each was measured end to end on a module set that does migrate: `_lifecycle` is composed by the platform itself, so the boot no longer refuses with `not-shipped: _lifecycle`; `pnpm run module:install --all` exists, is named by the command's own next steps and by the generated README, and is run by this criterion between `migrate` and `start` (39 modules in 5.6 s, measured); and the `[i18n] reconcile complete` line this assertion requires now appears (`installed=36 skipped=4 failed=0`). TWO BLOCKERS REMAIN BEHIND A3 AND BOTH ARE REPORTED TO THE ORCHESTRATOR. (1) `catalog`'s boot hook resolves `promptActionToolRegistry`, a plain registration `prompt_actions` owns, and the default set does not ship `prompt_actions` — a `contributes-to` edge is classified for an owner that is switched off, not for one that was never composed, so the boot dies with an `AwilixResolutionError`. (2) Of the 23 container names `backend/src/composition.ts` contributes, 22 are not contributed by `composeApp`, and roughly ten of those are not defaulted by the module that resolves them — `newsletterBridge` is the one this run reaches. That is `specs/117-instance-bring-up/` FR-030/FR-031 and T118's remaining drain: an instance supplies no contribute callback (R2.4), so every one of those names is absent in a client's tree.

A5.reason: The built admin bundle names exactly the installed module packages that publish an admin layer — 23 of 30 installed, over 3.6 MiB of JavaScript, measured on the bundle and not on the registry that produced it. The expectation is read off each installed package's own `exports` map and the evidence off the bundle, which is two authors on purpose, as `evaluateA3` already recomputes the migration order rather than reading the one the platform logged. T138 wrote the member; what it also needed was `endora generate`, because the renderer of `contracts/instance-tree.md` §2.6's two artefacts lived in `backend/scripts` and no client can reach it.

A6.reason: GREEN, AND IT LANDED RED. Measured: the built site serves 72 pages and its navigation names a routed page for exactly the 27 of 30 installed module packages that ship a `docs/` layer, both directions. The navigation half was clean from the first measurement — T137 wrote the documentation member (`contracts/instance-tree.md` §2.4a) and moved the renderers into `@endora-commerce/cli` — and what was red was the **build**, under `onBrokenLinks: 'throw'`, over four broken links of two kinds. Three were a module page linking this repository's own site tree (`../architecture/custom-fields.md`, `../integrations/api-access.md`): refused by nothing in the estate, and broken in **every** instance whatever its module set, because a page above the modules category is the site's own content and travels with no package. 8 such links stood in 6 module packages. They are repaired and locked at zero by `check:module-docs`' `site-tree-link`, which carries no ledger because there is no instance in which such a link resolves (`specs/conventions/check-inventory.md`; `specs/conventions/module-documentation.md` item 1b). The fourth was the other kind — `catalog`'s `attributes.md` -> `../search.md`, a sibling the default set does not install — and it drained with them: `backend/scripts/ledgers/foreign-module-links/catalog.ts` keeps `promotions`, which that set does install. WHAT KEEPS IT GREEN IS NOT THIS RECORD. `site-tree-link` refuses the first kind outright, and `foreign-module-link`'s two-way shards refuse an unledgered one of the second — but a *ledgered* sibling link in a module the default set installs would pass every check in the estate and red this assertion, which is the case `specs/100-module-owned-documentation/`'s Phase 2 drain exists for and the reason A6 is worth running rather than inferring.

A7.reason: Two of its three halves are the API surface and the module enumeration, and both are A4's — the instance does not boot. The third, the built admin bundle, now has a subject and A5 asserts it in one direction (a module named in the bundle and not installed is A5's `extra`), so what is left here is a third of the assertion. It waits on A4, and A4 on A3. T142 is the row.

A8.reason: It needs a booted instance (A4) and a divergence report, and it has neither. T137 wrote the documentation member, which is the half A6 was waiting on, and reconciled the file manifest (`packages/cli/test/new-instance/manifest-reconciliation.test.ts`). THE DIVERGENCE REPORT IS STILL NOBODY'S: `contracts/instance-tree.md` §2.6 lists three generated artefacts and it is not among them, and its renderer is `backend/scripts/generate-divergence.ts` over `backend/scripts/lib/divergence.ts` — 511 + 1200 lines reading this repository's own overlay resolver, its module layout and a port->owner map built from module *sources*, none of which an instance has. Moving it is the shape T137 and T138 gave the other two artefact families and is a task of its own. The boot half is A4's, behind D-226.

A9.reason: It needs a booted instance with a migrated schema to read across tenants in — A4, and A3 below it. `contracts/instance-repository.md` R6.3 is the assertion; T141 is the task that turns it green.

A10.reason: A module set missing a required module is refused with exit 1, the target directory untouched, and the refusal carries verbatim the `activation.reason` an installed manifest declares — which is what R5.6 and D-100 ask for and what an exit-code check alone would not see. The sentences are read out of the packages this run resolved, never from a list in the criterion.

A11.reason: Both halves have a subject now: `@endora-commerce/platform` and `@endora-commerce/admin-shell` both resolve in the created instance, and none of the 27 files the command wrote is byte-identical to any of the 1036 those two packages ship. The counts are printed by the run rather than recorded here. Two things had to change for the second half to stop being vacuous: T138 wrote the admin member that depends on the shell, and the criterion learned to look for a package in a **member's** `node_modules` as well as the root's — pnpm installs a package where it is declared, so reading the root alone reported `admin-shell does not resolve` over a tree that had it.

A12.reason: It needs a fixture registry to publish a platform patch into and a second install to pick it up. T144, gated on F10 (`specs/071-modular-packaging/roadmap.md`).

A13.reason: 174 KiB of built stylesheet carries, for each of 16 packages — the shell and 15 module admin layers — a class only that package uses, so its presence can only be explained by that package's own sources having been scanned. A5 says the screens are in the bundle; this says they are visible. Three exclusions keep the witness honest and each was measured rather than reasoned: a token is read only out of a `class`/`className` position (every string literal made i18n keys and DOM ids look like classes and reported seven modules as unscanned), a class the design system's own imported `theme.css` defines is evidence of nothing in either direction, and a token carrying a `.` is escaped in the compiled CSS and could never be matched. A package with no class of its own is counted and skipped, never failed.

A14.reason: 242 lines of wiring across the 12 files the command classified as wiring, counted on disk in the created tree rather than on the plan, against R1.4's bound of 250. IT WAS 241 BEFORE T137 and the one line is `pnpm-workspace.yaml`'s third member: §2.4a's four files are all `client` or `derived` — the Docusaurus configuration and the sidebar are the client's in `admin/vite.config.ts`' and `admin/src/index.css`' sense, and the manifest is derived — so the documentation member adds no wiring of its own. 8 lines of headroom.

history: 2026-09-11 — T140. The criterion lands: `scripts/acceptance/instance.ts`, its judgement in
`scripts/acceptance/instance-assertions.ts`, this record and the `acceptance:instance` job.
First measurement on `master` at 55bebe991, mode `tarball`: 4 pass, 2 fail, 8 unmeasured.
The two reds are defects in the product, not in the contracts, and they are the reason the
row exists: A3 found that every root script of a scaffolded instance matches no project
and exits 0, so `migrate`, `build` and `start` are successful no-ops. Three further
defects behind it are recorded in A4's reason, each measured by hand on a repaired tree.
Nothing here is fixed by this merge request: the instrument's own merge request is not
the place to also repair what it finds.
2026-09-11 — T141. Four of the five defects the first run found are repaired, in
`@endora-commerce/platform` and `@endora-commerce/cli`. Measured on `master` at d49e6d1f5:
mode `tarball`, 4 pass, 1 fail, 9 unmeasured. A3 stays red and A4 moves from `fail` to
`unmeasured`, and neither is a regression: the migrate step used to exit 0 having matched
no project, and now it runs and fails on the one defect T141 did not take — the platform's
own migration corpus is not self-contained. A14 moves from 204 lines to 230, inside the
same bound, because the five operator commands now dispose what they opened. The repairs,
each verified end to end on a module set that does migrate: root scripts reach the member;
an instance runs the platform's own twelve migrations and registers its six entities;
`_lifecycle` is composed by the platform rather than by a generated index no instance has;
`module:install --all` exists and is documented; and the operator commands no longer hang.
2026-09-12 — T138, the admin member. Measured on the feature branch: mode `tarball`, 7 pass,
1 fail, 6 unmeasured. A5, A11 and A13 move from `unmeasured` to `pass` and A14 from 230 lines to
241, inside the same bound. A3 is unchanged and is still the one red: the platform's own
migration corpus is not self-contained, which is a schema decision and not this row's. A4 is
unchanged behind it. A7's reason is narrower than it was, because one of its three halves now has
a subject. Two defects the member's own build found, both repaired here and neither visible to a
source-tree check: a module package's optional peers were declared by nobody in a scaffolded
instance, so Vite bound them to `__vite-optional-peer-dep:` stubs and the whole admin bundle
failed on a named import; and `mod-settings` statically imported `mod-credentials`' preview modal,
which takes out every module's screens in any instance that did not install `credentials`.
